systems.name: Voice-Leading Taxonomy System
systems.summary: Governs how voice-leading types are classified and applied. Establishes GDVL as the diatonic foundation, positions SCVL as the chromatic superstructure, and treats IVL and FVL as specialized instances of SCVL. Melody and harmony are held as equals throughout.

members.name: GDVL (Generic Diatonic Voice-Leading)
members.summary: The foundational diatonic voice-leading mode covering Volumes 1 and 2.

members.name: SCVL (Specific Chromatic Voice-Leading)
members.summary: The chromatic voice-leading superstructure. IVL and FVL are specialized sub-instances of SCVL.

members.name: IVL (Intervallic Voice-Leading)
members.summary: Voice-leading defined by interval relationships; a specialized instance of SCVL.

members.name: FVL (Functional Voice-Leading)
members.summary: Voice-leading defined by harmonic function; a specialized instance of SCVL.

members.name: M.S.R.P. (Melodic Strand Replication Procedure)
members.summary: A procedural technique for replicating melodic strands across voices.

traversal_rules.name: Diatonic Foundation Before Chromatic Extension
traversal_rules.summary: GDVL must be established as the operating mode before SCVL is introduced.

references.quote_excerpt: IVLs and FVLs are all examples of SCVL, as opposed to GDVL

traversal_rules.name: IVL/FVL Traversed as SCVL Sub-Types
traversal_rules.summary: IVL or FVL passages must be classified as operating within SCVL.

references.quote_excerpt: The IVLs and the FVLs are all examples of SCVL

traversal_rules.name: Melodic and Harmonic Domains Traversed as Equals
traversal_rules.summary: No traversal path may privilege melody over harmony or vice versa.

references.topic: Author's position: melody and harmony as equals
references.quote_excerpt: excellent voice-leading treats both melody and harmony as equals

modification_rules.name: Grip-Slipping Technique Application
modification_rules.summary: A named fretboard technique that modifies how a voicing is physically executed.

references.quote_excerpt: grip-slipping: more on this later

systems.name: Event / Episode Modal Transposition System
systems.summary: Governs the generative transposition of Events and Episodes across diatonic and modal space. An Event diatonically transposed yields up to 6 variants (some intervallic collapses); an Episode diatonically transposed yields exactly 6 variants with one-to-one modal correspondence.

members.name: Event
members.summary: Discrete musical unit; diatonically transposed to yield up to 6 others, some collapsing.

members.name: Episode
members.summary: Musical unit transposable to 6 others, each corresponding to a mode.

traversal_rules.name: Event Diatonic Transposition — Six-Step Rule
traversal_rules.summary: Diatonic transposition up to 6 steps; intervallically identical transpositions collapse to a single representative.

references.quote_excerpt: an event can be diatonically transposed to create 6 other events
but some of them will be intervallically identical

traversal_rules.name: Episode Modal Correspondence — One-to-One Rule
traversal_rules.summary: Episode transposition produces 7 modal variants without collapse.

references.quote_excerpt: each corresponds to a different mode

references.topic: Diatonic transposition of episodes and modal correspondence
references.quote_excerpt: an episode can be diatonically transposed to create 6 other episodes

traversal_rules.name: Domain-Agnostic Routing of Events and Episodes
traversal_rules.summary: Events and Episodes are routed identically across melodic, contrapuntal, and harmonic domains.

references.quote_excerpt: Both events and episodes can be melodic, contrapuntal, harmonic

references.topic: Melodic/contrapuntal/harmonic scope of events and episodes
references.quote_excerpt: or in any combination

modification_rules.name: Length Is Not a Defining Modifier
modification_rules.summary: Event vs Episode is classified by note coverage, not by length.

references.quote_excerpt: events as being shorter, while episodes are longer

modification_rules.name: Sus4 Chord Label Required Over C2/Add-2
modification_rules.summary: Sus4 labeling enforced over shorter notations; applies to 3-part and 4-part 4ths and all inversions.

references.topic: Naming rationale for sus4 chord nomenclature
references.quote_excerpt: My suggestion for a suitable name for this chord would be: G [sus4]

references.topic: Naming sus4 chords vs C2 notation
references.quote_excerpt: I will grant you that C2 is shorter, but
Of course, this applies to all of the inversions as well

systems.name: Chord Construction and Catalog System
systems.summary: Governs all chord derivation, density management, and catalog organization. 3-part chords derived from 4-part by single-voice omission; each type appears exactly 4 times. The catalog is organized by cycle-3/cycle-4 alternation across 24 voicings × 35 chord types = 840 voicings. 3-part chords prioritized for playability; exercises anchor in C Major before student-driven transposition.

members.name: 4-Part Chord
members.summary: Source voicing for 3-part derivation; the density ceiling.

members.name: 3-Part Chord
members.summary: Derived by removing one voice from a 4-part chord.

members.name: Expanded M-Lode Taxonomy
members.summary: Volume 2's M-Lode plus three new 3-part types.

traversal_rules.name: 3-Part Chords Take Traversal Priority Over 4-Part
traversal_rules.summary: Route through 3-part chords before 4-part chords for fretboard playability.

references.quote_excerpt: 3-part chords are easier to play than 4-part chords

traversal_rules.name: Cycle-3 / Cycle-4 Alternation as Master Organizing Principle
traversal_rules.summary: All traversal through the chord catalog follows cycle-3/cycle-4 alternation.

references.quote_excerpt: this same approach could be applied to pretty much everything

traversal_rules.name: C Major as Presentation Anchor; Transposition by Student
traversal_rules.summary: All catalog exercises presented in C Major; transposition is student responsibility.

references.topic: Scope and scale options for the chapter material
references.quote_excerpt: presented in C Major (no accidentals)
developed the necessary skills to make the needed adjustments

modification_rules.name: Derive 3-Part Chords by Single Voice Omission
modification_rules.summary: Removing exactly one voice from a 4-part chord yields a 3-part chord; each type appears 4 times.

references.topic: Method premise: deriving 3-part chords from 4-part chords
references.quote_excerpt: arrive at different 3-part chords by leaving out one voice

references.topic: Symmetry observation: each 3-part chord type appears four times
references.quote_excerpt: Each 3-part chord appears four times

modification_rules.name: Expand M-Lode With Three New 3-Part Chord Types
modification_rules.summary: Add 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), and 3-part Spread Clusters to the taxonomy.

references.topic: The Real Compleat M-Lode — expanded structure
references.quote_excerpt: we add 3 different 3-part chords: 7th (no 3rd), 7th (no 5th), 3-part Spread Clusters

modification_rules.name: 4-Part Voicing Is the Density Ceiling
modification_rules.summary: No chord construction exceeds 4 parts; density reduces downward via voice omission.

references.topic: Method premise: deriving 3-part chords from 4-part chords
references.quote_excerpt: leaving out one voice of a 4-part chord

modification_rules.name: Passing Tones and Melodic Embellishment on 3-Part Voicings
modification_rules.summary: 3-part chord voicings may be modified with passing tones and embellishments within the C Major anchor.

references.topic: Scope and scale options for the chapter material
references.quote_excerpt: All of the material that follows in this next section will be presented in C Major
